blocks.x: What Data & Lakehouse changes inside Agriculture & Food Systems: the processes we target, the controls we inherit, the platforms underneath, and the measured delta at every gate.

In Agriculture & Food Systems, data, analytics & lakehouse is the substrate tower: pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture on databricks and snowflake, streaming and event-driven decisioning, executive bi, master data and cataloging, predictive analytics, and data products that generate revenue. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: data engineering & pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture & migration, real-time streaming & event-driven decisioning — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Chain data broken at every handoff
Farm, co-op, processor and retail data never join; traceability requires weeks of document archaeology.
Lenders and insurers price farms on history, not practice; sustainable practice earns no capital advantage.
Agronomic decisions run on tradition because soil, weather and crop telemetry are patchy; input spend is uniform where it should be variable.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

Delivery composes 7 services from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower — Data Engineering & Pipeline Modernization, Lakehouse Architecture & Migration, Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning, Enterprise BI & Executive Analytics as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method, with EUDR obligations shaping the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Resilient, observable pipelines: trusted data from source to decision at SLA.
Lakehouse the right way: Unity Catalog governance, cost-aware design and AI-ready foundations.
Decisions at event speed: sub-second pipelines from sensor, click or transaction to action.
Metrics into management: one governed semantic layer, decision cadence built in.
Field, machine, weather and lab data unified with plot-level lineage (agronomy and finance on the same truth)
Custody events from plot to pallet with master-data discipline (recall queries answered in minutes)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: EUDR and EUDR. Deforestation-free due diligence with geolocation evidence for in-scope commodities. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The rhythm is fixed on purpose: progress becomes visible from week one, not after the first steering meeting. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
